details:
**Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun**
Claude Debussy's 1894 symphonic poem, inspired by a poem by Stéphane Mallarmé and often seen as the start of modern music. It opens with a famous unaccompanied flute solo that slides chromatically down from C-sharp to G (a tritone) and back up. Georges Barrère played the solo at the premiere.

**The Magic Flute**
Mozart's 1791 Singspiel (Die Zauberflöte), with a libretto by the Freemason Emanuel Schikaneder. Prince Tamino receives the enchanted flute from the Three Ladies, and its music protects him and Pamina during the trials of fire and water. The bird-catcher Papageno gets magic bells, and the Queen of the Night orders her daughter Pamina to kill the priest Sarastro in the coloratura aria "Der Hölle Rache."

**Boléro**
Maurice Ravel's 1928 orchestral piece, commissioned as a ballet by the dancer Ida Rubinstein. It is built on a snare-drum ostinato that runs through the whole work, and the flute is the first instrument to play the repeating melody, entering over the snare drum.

**Syrinx**
Debussy's short 1913 piece for unaccompanied flute, a cornerstone of the solo repertoire. It is named after the nymph who was turned into reeds that the god Pan made into his pan pipes, and it was the first important solo piece written for the modern Boehm flute.

**"Morning Mood"**
The opening movement of Edvard Grieg's Peer Gynt Suite No. 1. The flute plays a serene pastoral melody in E major (B, G-sharp, F-sharp, E, F-sharp, G-sharp), which the oboe then answers.

**Peter and the Wolf**
Sergei Prokofiev's 1936 children's piece for narrator and orchestra, in which each character is represented by an instrument. The flute plays the chirping bird, who argues with the duck (the oboe). The flute is also often used elsewhere to imitate birdsong.

**Density 21.5**
Edgard Varèse's 1936 piece for solo flute, written for Georges Barrère's new platinum flute. Its title refers to the density of platinum, about 21.5 grams per cubic centimeter.

**Theobald Boehm**
The 19th-century German flutist and inventor who designed the modern flute's key mechanism, the Boehm system. It uses ring keys, interlinked rods, and acoustically placed tone holes, and it was later adapted to the clarinet and oboe.

**Cécile Chaminade's Concertino**
The French composer's Concertino in D major, Op. 107 (1902), commissioned by the Paris Conservatoire as an exam piece for flute students. It is a standard part of the flute repertoire.

**Frederick the Great and Johann Quantz**
King Frederick II of Prussia was an accomplished flutist. His teacher Johann Joachim Quantz wrote a famous treatise on playing the transverse flute. J.S. Bach dedicated The Musical Offering to Frederick, and its trio sonata is scored for flute, violin, and continuo.

**Badinerie**
The fast, virtuosic final movement of J.S. Bach's Orchestral Suite No. 2 in B minor, in which the flute plays the lead melody. Bach also gave the flute a prominent role in Brandenburg Concerto No. 5.

**Mozart's flute concertos**
Mozart wrote Flute Concertos No. 1 in G major and No. 2 in D major, as well as the Concerto for Flute and Harp in C major, his only work featuring the harp. In letters to his father he complained that he disliked writing for the flute.

**Paul Taffanel**
The 19th-century French flutist and teacher who founded the French flute school, known for its light, flexible tone. He compiled the 17 Daily Exercises (with his student Philippe Gaubert), and his students included Georges Barrère.

**James Galway and Jean-Pierre Rampal**
Two of the most famous modern flute soloists. Galway is a Northern Irish virtuoso nicknamed "The Man with the Golden Flute," and Rampal was a French flutist known for playing a gold flute and for reviving Baroque flute music.

**Poulenc's Flute Sonata**
Francis Poulenc's Sonata for Flute and Piano, FP 164 (1957), one of the most frequently performed 20th-century flute works. Its first movement is marked Allegro malinconico. Other repertoire staples include Gabriel Fauré's Fantaisie and Olivier Messiaen's Le merle noir ("The Blackbird").
